stem: In which SDLC phase should security requirements FIRST be defined?

options.A: Testing, once the application is feature complete and ready for review
options.B: Deployment, when the operations team configures the production servers
options.C: Maintenance, after the first round of user feedback has been collected
options.D: Requirements gathering, alongside the functional requirements

explanation: Security requirements belong with functional requirements from the start, so design, coding, and testing can all build toward them.

distractor_rationales.A: Defining requirements at testing time means rework and missed controls.
distractor_rationales.B: Deployment is too late to shape the design.
distractor_rationales.C: Maintenance is far too late; flaws are already built in.

stem: Which development methodology completes each phase fully before the next phase begins?

options.A: Waterfall
options.B: Agile with two-week sprints and a continuously reprioritized backlog
options.C: Spiral, which repeats planning, risk analysis, and building in cycles
options.D: DevOps with continuous integration and frequent automated deployments

explanation: Waterfall is sequential: requirements, design, implementation, testing, and deployment each finish before the next starts.

distractor_rationales.B: Agile works in short iterations that overlap these activities.
distractor_rationales.C: Spiral repeats phases in risk-driven loops.
distractor_rationales.D: DevOps delivers continuously rather than in sequential phases.

stem: Which software security maturity model is built from observing the practices that real organizations actually perform?

options.A: The Capability Maturity Model Integration for general process improvement
options.B: BSIMM
options.C: The OWASP Top 10 list of common web application risks
options.D: The Common Criteria framework for evaluating security products

explanation: BSIMM is descriptive: it reports what many organizations actually do, so a company can compare itself with peers. SAMM, by contrast, is prescriptive.

distractor_rationales.A: CMMI is a general process maturity model, not built from software security observations.
distractor_rationales.C: The OWASP Top 10 is an awareness list of risks, not a maturity model.
distractor_rationales.D: Common Criteria evaluates products, not an organization's practices.

stem: What is the BEST control to stop unreviewed code from being merged into the main branch?

options.A: Ask developers to announce their merges in the team chat channel each day
options.B: Run a weekly report of all commits made to the main branch for managers
options.C: Branch protection that requires an approved review before merging
options.D: Give only senior developers access to the repository's issue tracker

explanation: Branch protection enforces the rule in the platform itself: nothing merges to main without an approved review and passing checks.

distractor_rationales.A: Announcements are informal and easily skipped.
distractor_rationales.B: A weekly report detects problems after the code is merged.
distractor_rationales.D: Issue tracker access does not control merges.

stem: What should a web application show users when an unexpected error occurs?

options.A: The full stack trace so that users can include it in their support tickets
options.B: The database query that failed, so users can see exactly what went wrong
options.C: The server's file path and software versions to help with troubleshooting
options.D: A generic message, with details logged on the server

explanation: Detailed errors reveal internals that help attackers. A generic message keeps users informed, while server-side logs keep the detail for developers.

distractor_rationales.A: Stack traces expose code structure and libraries.
distractor_rationales.B: Showing queries can reveal schema and aid injection.
distractor_rationales.C: Paths and versions help attackers target known flaws.

stem: A code review finds a production database password written directly in a source file. What is the BEST fix?

options.A: Load it from a secrets manager at runtime and rotate the exposed password
options.B: Move the password to a comment in the same file so it is not executed as code
options.C: Encode the password in Base64 so that it is not readable at a glance in the file
options.D: Rename the variable that holds the password to something less obvious to readers

explanation: Secrets belong in a secrets manager, not in code. Because the password was in source control, it must also be rotated.

distractor_rationales.B: A comment is still in the file and in version history.
distractor_rationales.D: Renaming the variable does not hide the value.

stem: A public login API receives millions of password guesses per day from automated tools. What is the BEST control?

options.A: Return more detailed error messages so that real users can fix their typos faster
options.B: Rate limiting per account and per client
options.C: Move the login API to a different URL path and tell only real customers about it
options.D: Increase the server capacity so the API can respond faster under heavy load

explanation: Rate limiting slows automated guessing to the point where it is ineffective, while legitimate users are unaffected.

distractor_rationales.A: Detailed errors help attackers learn which accounts exist.
distractor_rationales.C: A new path is obscurity and will be rediscovered.
distractor_rationales.D: More capacity lets attackers guess even faster.

stem: Which practice ensures that the code deployed to production is exactly the code that was tested?

options.A: Rebuilding the application from source separately in each environment before deploying it
options.B: Letting developers copy updated files directly to the production servers when needed
options.C: Promoting the same signed build artifact through each environment
options.D: Asking testers to email a summary of their results to the operations team

explanation: Building once and promoting the same signed artifact from test to production means the tested bits are the deployed bits.

distractor_rationales.A: Separate rebuilds can differ due to changed dependencies or settings.
distractor_rationales.B: Direct copies bypass testing and change control.
distractor_rationales.D: A summary email does not link results to what is deployed.

stem: A team has moved from six-month projects to two-week sprints, but the security team still does one review at the end of each release. What change BEST fits security into the new process?

options.A: Keep the single end-of-release review and simply make the review team larger
options.B: Stop security reviews entirely, since agile teams deliver too quickly for them
options.C: Hold a two-day security review at the end of every sprint that blocks all merges
options.D: Add security stories to the backlog and security criteria to the definition of done

explanation: Making security part of the backlog and the definition of done builds it into every sprint, rather than treating it as a late gate.

distractor_rationales.A: A larger team still reviews too late.
distractor_rationales.C: Long blocking reviews each sprint slow delivery and encourage workarounds.

stem: An internal application is being retired. Which security activity is MOST important in the disposal phase?

options.A: Archive or destroy its data per retention rules and revoke its credentials and integrations
options.B: Leave the servers running in case users need to look something up later on
options.C: Delete the application's source code repository first to save on hosting costs
options.D: Send a company-wide email announcing the date that the application is going away

explanation: Retirement must handle the data according to retention rules and remove the accounts, keys, and connections the application used, so nothing is left behind for attackers.

distractor_rationales.B: Forgotten running servers become unpatched targets.
distractor_rationales.C: Deleting source code is not the priority and may be needed for records.
distractor_rationales.D: An announcement is helpful but does not address security.

stem: A SAMM assessment scores an organization low across nearly every practice. What is the BEST way to proceed?

options.A: Aim for the highest maturity level in every practice within the next year
options.B: Set targets for a few high-priority practices and improve step by step
options.C: Discard the results, since low scores show that the model does not fit the company
options.D: Wait until the budget allows the company to improve every practice at once

explanation: Maturity models are meant for incremental progress. Choosing a few high-impact practices and raising them step by step delivers results and builds momentum.

distractor_rationales.A: Trying to max out every practice at once is unrealistic.
distractor_rationales.C: Low scores are the reason to use the model, not to reject it.
distractor_rationales.D: Waiting for a perfect budget delays all improvement.

stem: Developers keep committing API keys to repositories by accident. Which control BEST prevents new occurrences?

options.A: A quarterly reminder email that tells developers not to commit any secrets
options.B: A monthly manual review of every repository by the security team
options.C: Pre-commit secret scanning plus server-side push protection
options.D: Making every repository private so that the keys are not publicly visible

explanation: Scanning at commit time and blocking pushes that contain secrets stops them before they enter history, which is far cheaper than cleaning up later.

distractor_rationales.B: Monthly manual review finds secrets long after they are exposed.
distractor_rationales.D: Private repositories still expose keys to everyone with access and to anyone who breaches them.

stem: A public project's CI pipeline runs automatically on pull requests from forks, and those jobs can read the deployment secrets. What is the BEST fix?

options.A: Ask contributors to promise in writing that they will not print the secrets in logs
options.B: Rotate the deployment secrets once a month so that any leaked copies expire
options.C: Move the deployment secrets into a file stored in the same repository instead
options.D: Withhold secrets from untrusted fork builds and require approval to run them

explanation: Code from a fork is untrusted. It should run without secrets, and privileged workflows should run only after a maintainer approves.

distractor_rationales.A: A promise does not stop malicious code in the pull request.
distractor_rationales.B: Monthly rotation still leaves secrets exposed to anyone who submits a pull request.
distractor_rationales.C: Secrets in the repository are worse.

stem: Software composition analysis flags a critical vulnerability in a library, but the vulnerable function is never called by the application. How should the team handle the finding?

options.A: Lower its priority based on reachability and schedule the upgrade
options.B: Close it permanently, since the vulnerable function is not used by the application today
options.C: Stop all releases immediately until the library has been removed from every application
options.D: Ignore all future SCA results, since findings like this one are clearly unreliable

explanation: Reachability and exploitability should shape priority. The finding is real, so the upgrade should still be scheduled, but it need not block urgent work.

distractor_rationales.B: The code could start calling the function later, so the finding should not be closed permanently.
distractor_rationales.C: Halting all releases is disproportionate for an unreachable flaw.
distractor_rationales.D: One lower-priority finding does not make the tool unreliable.

stem: An attacker publishes a public package with the same name as a company's internal package, but a higher version number, and the build system downloads it. What is this attack called?

options.A: Typosquatting on a misspelled package name
options.B: Dependency confusion
options.C: A buffer overflow in the package manager's parser
options.D: Cross-site request forgery against the repository site

explanation: Dependency confusion exploits build tools that prefer the highest version across public and private registries. Pinning, scoped names, and private registry precedence prevent it.

distractor_rationales.A: Typosquatting relies on misspelled names, not identical ones.
distractor_rationales.D: CSRF targets web sessions, not build dependency resolution.

stem: A company depends on a critical application from a small vendor that may not stay in business. Which contract provision BEST protects the company?

options.A: A clause requiring the vendor to send a monthly newsletter about product updates
options.B: A discount on license fees if the vendor misses its product roadmap deadlines
options.C: A source code escrow agreement with defined release conditions
options.D: A promise from the vendor's CEO that the company is financially stable

explanation: Escrow places the source code with a neutral third party, to be released to the customer if the vendor fails, so the software can still be maintained.

distractor_rationales.B: A discount does not help if the vendor disappears.
distractor_rationales.D: A verbal assurance is not enforceable protection.

stem: A download endpoint takes a filename parameter. A tester requests "../../etc/passwd" and receives the system password file. What is the BEST root-cause fix?

options.A: Block requests that contain the word "passwd" at the web application firewall
options.B: Run the web server under an account with a longer and more complex password
options.C: Rename the system password file to something that attackers will not guess
options.D: Map requests to allow-listed file IDs, or canonicalize paths and check the base directory

explanation: Path traversal happens when user input builds file paths. Using indirect IDs, or resolving the path and confirming it stays inside the allowed directory, removes the flaw.

distractor_rationales.A: Blocking one keyword is easily bypassed and does not fix the code.
distractor_rationales.B: Account passwords do not affect path handling.
distractor_rationales.C: Renaming system files breaks the system and leaves other files exposed.

stem: An ordinary user discovers that calling the API endpoint /admin/deleteUser directly succeeds, even though the admin menu is hidden in the app. What weakness is this?

options.A: Broken function-level authorization
options.B: Insecure transport caused by a missing TLS configuration on the API gateway
options.C: A denial-of-service weakness from missing rate limits on the endpoint
options.D: Improper output encoding that allows scripts to run in the user's browser

explanation: The server does not check whether the caller's role permits the administrative function. Hiding the menu in the client is not access control.

distractor_rationales.B: The issue is authorization, not encryption in transit.
distractor_rationales.C: Rate limits do not decide who may call a function.
distractor_rationales.D: Output encoding addresses XSS, not authorization.

stem: What is the BEST way to reduce the risk of a major release to a large customer-facing application?

options.A: Release to every user at once late on a Friday so traffic is low over the weekend
options.B: A staged rollout to a small share of users, with monitoring and a tested rollback
options.C: Skip testing for this release, since the previous release went smoothly
options.D: Let each developer deploy their own changes whenever they finish them

explanation: A staged (canary) rollout exposes a small group first, so problems are caught early and rolled back before they reach everyone.

distractor_rationales.A: A full Friday release maximizes impact and reduces staff to respond.
distractor_rationales.C: Past success does not validate new code.

stem: The private key used to sign the company's software releases is stored as a file on the build server, readable by every pipeline job. What is the BEST improvement?

options.A: Encrypt the key file with a password stored in a text file next to it on the server
options.B: Copy the key to each developer's laptop so that signing does not depend on one server
options.C: Move signing to an HSM or managed signing service, allowed only for release jobs
options.D: Change the name of the key file each month so that attackers cannot find it easily

explanation: If an attacker can use the signing key, they can sign malware as the company. A hardware-backed signing service limited to approved release jobs protects the key and logs every use.

distractor_rationales.A: A password stored next to the file protects nothing.
distractor_rationales.B: Spreading the key to laptops multiplies exposure.

stem: A critical flaw is announced in a widely used logging library. Leadership asks which of the company's 300 applications are affected. What makes this question fastest to answer?

options.A: Emailing every development team and waiting for them to reply with their answers
options.B: Scanning the internet for public reports that mention the company's products
options.C: Waiting for each vendor to publish its own advisory before starting any analysis
options.D: Querying current SBOMs for the affected component and version

explanation: SBOMs list every component and version in each application, so a query identifies exposure in minutes rather than days.

distractor_rationales.A: Manual surveys are slow and incomplete.
distractor_rationales.B: Public reports will not list internal applications.
distractor_rationales.C: Waiting for vendors delays response for in-house software.

stem: A profile update API accepts a JSON body and binds all fields to the user object. A tester adds "role": "admin" to the request and gains administrator rights. What is the BEST root-cause fix?

options.A: Bind only an allow-list of editable fields on the server
options.B: Hide the role field in the web form so that users do not see it on the page
options.C: Log every profile update so that role changes can be reviewed later on
options.D: Add a CAPTCHA to the profile page to stop automated tools from sending requests

explanation: Mass assignment occurs when the server binds whatever fields the client sends. Explicitly allowing only editable fields prevents privilege fields from being set by users.

distractor_rationales.B: Hiding a field in the client does not stop crafted requests.
distractor_rationales.C: Logging detects the abuse but does not prevent it.
distractor_rationales.D: A CAPTCHA does not stop a manual attacker from adding a field.

stem: A SaaS vendor will not allow customers to run penetration tests against its platform. The service will hold sensitive customer data. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Test the platform anyway without informing the vendor, since the data is sensitive
options.B: Rely on independent attestations and contract terms for security and breach notice
options.C: Accept the service without any assurance, because SaaS providers handle security
options.D: Reject all SaaS vendors that decline customer penetration tests, however critical

explanation: When direct testing is not allowed, the customer can rely on independent reports such as SOC 2 Type II and recent third-party test summaries, and back them with contractual security requirements and notification deadlines.

distractor_rationales.A: Testing without permission may be illegal and breach the contract.
distractor_rationales.C: Shared responsibility still requires the customer to seek assurance.
distractor_rationales.D: A blanket rejection ignores other sound ways to get assurance.

stem: A DAST scan in the pipeline reports no findings, but a review shows it only ever reached the login page. What is the BEST correction?

options.A: Run the same scan more often so that it has more chances to find issues
options.B: Replace DAST with a manual review of the login page's HTML source
options.C: Configure authenticated scanning with a test account and session handling
options.D: Accept the results, since no findings means the application is secure

explanation: A scanner that cannot log in tests almost nothing. Giving it a dedicated test account and handling sessions lets it crawl and test the authenticated application.

distractor_rationales.A: Repeating an unauthenticated scan still reaches only the login page.
distractor_rationales.B: Reviewing one page's source does not test the application.
distractor_rationales.D: Zero findings reflects the missing coverage, not security.

stem: A developer wrote a custom encryption algorithm for customer data because standard libraries "seemed too complex." What should the security team require?

options.A: Keep the custom algorithm but keep its design secret so attackers cannot study it
options.B: Have the same developer write a second algorithm to encrypt the output again
options.C: Keep the custom algorithm, but increase its key size to 512 bits for extra strength
options.D: Replace it with a vetted library using a standard algorithm such as AES-GCM

explanation: Custom cryptography almost always has flaws that experts would find. Well-reviewed libraries implementing standard algorithms are far safer.

distractor_rationales.A: Secrecy of design is not security; strong algorithms are public.
distractor_rationales.B: Stacking two homemade algorithms does not make either one sound.
distractor_rationales.C: Key size cannot fix a flawed algorithm.
